How many party balloons would it take to lift you into the sky?
A balloon floats because helium is lighter than the air it pushes aside.
But one balloon only lifts about ten grams, about as much as two coins.
A grown-up weighs around seventy kilograms.
So you'd need roughly seven thousand balloons, a bunch bigger than a bus.
And as you rise, the air gets thinner and colder, and the balloons swell until they start to pop.
In 1982, a man tied about forty weather balloons to a lawn chair.
He floated nearly five kilometres up, cold and scared, and came down by popping them, one by one.
So yes, balloons can lift you. Getting down is the hard part.
